problems.title: Repeated queries mutate cached curvature eigenvalues
problems.source_location: Sections 2–3, PDF pp.3–5; Appendix C, PDF p.31; Appendix E, PDF pp.33–34; official supplement logix/analysis/influence_function_utils.py, precondition_kfac, lines 27–36
claim: For fixed cached eigenvalues \(D\) and explicit damping \(\lambda\), the influence preconditioner should use \((D+\lambda)^{-1}\) without changing the stored curvature.
analysis: In the same-device branch, the temporary tensor aliases the cache and damping is added in place. For a scalar eigenvalue and query gradient both equal to \(1\), with \(\lambda=0.1\), successive identical calls therefore return \(1/1.1\), \(1/1.2\), and \(1/1.3\), rather than the fixed value \(1/1.1\). Positive curvature, matching dimensions and same-device storage suffice; singularity is unnecessary.
result: The routine’s output can depend on prior query count. Whether the published experiments exercised that aliasing path is unresolved.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Keep \(D\) immutable and form \(D+\lambda\) out of place, or clone before an in-place update. This removes query-count dependence at this interface.
problems.impact_rationale: A local cache mutation is proved, but its prevalence or effect on central experimental conclusions is not established.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Default damping depends on layer enumeration order
problems.source_location: Appendix C, PDF p.31, damping definition; official supplement logix/analysis/influence_function_utils.py, precondition_kfac module loop
claim: Appendix C describes damping based on \(0.1\) times the mean eigenvalue. The release initializes the shared damping variable inside its module loop only while it is unset.
analysis: For scalar layers with eigenvalues \(1\) and \(100\), per-layer damping is \(0.1\) and \(10\). Processing the small layer first instead uses \(0.1\) for both; reversing the order uses \(10\) for both. The small layer’s output changes from \(1/1.1\) to \(1/11\) under a pure dictionary-order change. This is separate from cache mutation because the factorized branch creates fresh tensors.
result: The default preconditioner is not determined solely by each layer’s statistics and the declared damping policy.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Create a fresh \(\lambda_m=0.1\operatorname{mean}(D_m)\) for each layer, while preserving a user-supplied fixed value when provided. Do not overwrite the shared user option inside the loop.
problems.impact_rationale: The release implements an order-dependent default; the historical experiment setting and resulting scientific impact are unknown.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
